subject: general
question: 6 years ago, the age of a father was 40 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **son's age** 6 years ago be **x**. Then **father's age** was **2x + 40**.

The **age difference** between them was (2x + 40) − x = **x + 40**.

Since the age difference remains **constant**, when the father becomes **twice** the son's age, the difference must equal the son's age at that time.

So, at that future point, the son will be **x + 40** years old.

Current age of son = **x + 6**. Years from now = (x + 40) − (x + 6) = **34 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/236fdeab39a448e4b6f5dabdca7a39ab65451dd93e745cac823ea3f9b4772cd4.png] 

**Given:** 6 years ago, **Father (F−₆)** = 2 × **Son (S−₆)** + 40.

**Formula:** Age Difference (D) = Father's Age − Son's Age (always constant).

⇒ Let S−₆ = x. Then F−₆ = 2x + 40.

⇒ **Difference (D)** = (2x + 40) − x = x + 40.

⇒ Present ages: **Son** = x + 6, **Father** = 2x + 46.

⇒ In 'n' years from now, **Father** = 2 × **Son**.

⇒ (2x + 46 + n) = 2 × (x + 6 + n).

⇒ 2x + 46 + n = 2x + 12 + 2n.

⇒ 46 − 12 = 2n − n.

⇒ n = 34.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The numerical difference between the ages of two persons remains the same at any point in time.

Ratio of Ages

While age difference is constant, the ratio of ages changes as time passes (except when the difference is zero).

Future/Past Calculations

To find age 'n' years ago, subtract n. To find age 'n' years hence, add n to the present age.</p
